clue.text: Carping woman?

parts.note: reads as a nagging, complaining woman, but carping also suggests carp, the fish, so a woman who sells fish fits as well

explanation.surface: A question about a nagging, fault-finding woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The traditional seller of fish was famous for her loud, coarse scolding, so both senses of 'carping' meet in the one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-seller's wife was a byword for a shrill, abusive scold, so the word now means a nagging woman.

clue.text: Archaic interjection, for example, since "Jesus Christ!"

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks years counted since the birth of Christ

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation, like someone crying out the Lord's name.
explanation.walkthrough: "Jesus Christ!" reads as an oath, but it is the birth from which AD dates are counted.
explanation.definitionFit: An old mild oath of surprise, a softened form of 'by God', now heard only as a period piece.

clue.text: See 15
Paul left the Guardian almost totally in confusion

parts.note: Paul is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: almost all of the word is kept, its final letter being dropped

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over a person

explanation.surface: The setter claims to have quit the newspaper in a state of complete muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Guardian' looks like the newspaper Paul writes for; here it is a guardian ANGEL, cut to ANGE by 'almost totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture or jumble of different things, borrowed from French, so a confusion of elements.

clue.text: Radical protects political street fighter

indicators.note: radical change shakes things up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An extremist is shielding a brawling politician.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott, Britain's Deputy Prime Minister, famously punched a protester who threw an egg at him during the 2001 election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The British politician John Prescott was known for throwing a punch at an egg-throwing heckler in the street.

clue.text: See 24
Yankees to cage as animals

indicators.note: to cage means to enclose, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: in British betting a Yankee is a combined wager on four selections, so Yankees are bets

explanation.surface: A New York baseball team's players being locked up like zoo creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankees' points to Americans or the baseball team; here it is a bet placed with a British bookmaker, eleven wagers on four horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts are animals, especially large four-footed ones, as opposed to people.

clue.text: Compound of nitrogen with annoying effect?

indicators.note: a compound mixes elements together, so the letters of the next word are mixed

explanation.surface: A chemical compound containing nitrogen that has an irritating result.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface makes 'Compound' look like a substance; it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone's ring tone, heard going off in public, is a classic irritation.

clue.text: Island finding ways to communicate

indicators.note: communicating out loud means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: roads are ways for travelling along

explanation.surface: Discovering methods of getting a message across to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways to communicate' looks like a single phrase meaning methods of contact; 'to communicate' is the sound signal on 'ways'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, largest of the Dodecanese.

clue.text: See 19
Right about answer on poetry getting across

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters of right's abbreviation are read backwards

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A correct reply about some poems being understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Transverse means lying or extending across something, crosswise.

clue.text: See 24 down
Legal position for sailor, given year unable to sail around?

indicators.note: around means the outer phrase surrounds the others

parts.note: with no ship, one cannot sail
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman takes a job ashore after a year in which he could not put to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the sailor and year inside the phrase for being unable to sail; 'for' and 'given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a notary, a lawyer who certifies documents, is a post in the legal profession.

clue.text: Blimey, it's virtuous

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'my word!'
the quality of being good and upright, virtue itself

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a mild oath like 'goodness me' and the noun for moral virtue.

clue.text: Author who could balance a pint on her head while playing billiards, they say?

indicators.note: they say means the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.words: who could balance a pint on her head while playing billiards
parts.note: someone who does a trick while potting balls would be a trick ..., a woman described as 'be a trick ...'

explanation.surface: A writer with an unlikely talent for balancing beer while at the billiards table.
explanation.walkthrough: The description makes her a potter (one who pots balls) able to be a trick performer; spoken, 'be a trick potter' gives the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter wrote and illustrated The Tale of Peter Rabbit and other children's books.

clue.text: Opening point kept in mind, though not initially made up

indicators.note: kept in means placed inside the other piece
the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a vent is an opening
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An idea of an opening held in one's thoughts, though not created at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the first letter of mind, and 'kept in' places the opening and point inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invented has been made up, fabricated or devised rather than real.

clue.text: Matches turn on flat set

indicators.note: turn means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: fits is a synonym of matches, as in 'it fits the description'
a fen is flat marshland, as in the English Fens

explanation.surface: Games switch over to a level arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the synonym of 'Matches'; a fen is low-lying wetland, as in the Fens of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to become firm or rigid, as jelly or concrete does.

clue.text: The whole of eternity?

indicators.note: the question mark hints that the word is not taken at face value but rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether forever is everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety is the whole of something, all of it taken together.

clue.text: Country in favour of capital punishment — why Bush beat Gore?

parts.note: hanging is a form of capital punishment
Chad is a country in central Africa

explanation.surface: A nation supports the death penalty, which explains a presidential election result.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2000 US election, punch-card ballots with partly detached 'hanging chads' left Florida's count in dispute, and Bush won.
explanation.definitionFit: Disputed partly-punched ballots in Florida decided the 2000 election that Bush won over Gore.

clue.text: Sex symbol a little short getting through capital

indicators.note: a little short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe was the archetypal screen sex symbol
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A glamour star, slightly undersized, passing through a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Monrovia is the capital city of Liberia, in West Africa.

clue.text: Why I can never get a signal on my mobile phone network?

definitions.text: Why I can never get a signal on my mobile phone network?

parts.words: Why I can never get a signal on my mobile phone network?
parts.note: the network is also a UK brand named after a colour

explanation.surface: A grumble about poor mobile reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Orange was a British mobile phone network; split as O RANGE it means zero range.
explanation.definitionFit: A former British mobile phone network company, whose name split up means a range of nought.

clue.text: Independent leader into social equality

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a social is a party, a friendly gathering

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A non-party politician's head joins a social group seeking fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality, especially of status, pay or value.

clue.text: Extremes of price fixed with a coin of old

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A fixed price at both ends of the scale for an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Where priests found crime in book, perhaps

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: pages make up a book, so a book is an example of pages
arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: Clerics discovering a criminal act recorded in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' reads as 'discovered' with crime; it belongs to the definition, as in 'where priests are found'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is a house provided for a parish priest, so that is where clergy are to be found.

clue.text: The Elephant Man experienced suffering

definitions.meaning: the actor John ... played the title role in the 1980 film
to feel pain or distress, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: John Hurt starred in The Elephant Man, and the word is also past tense for felt pain.

clue.text: So might a cannibal entertain?

parts.note: hosting a guest at an evening meal, read literally for a man-eater, means serving the guest as the meal

explanation.surface: A question about how a man-eater would host guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means inviting a guest to the evening meal; for a cannibal the guest is the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for inviting a guest to a meal, taken literally for someone who eats people.

clue.text: I start to nap in holiday home, though light

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a gite is a rented holiday cottage in France

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone begins to doze in a French holiday cottage, lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective after 'though'; it is the verb, to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to set fire to it, to ignite it.

clue.text: Turned out well about infertility treatment female dismissed, one giving birth

indicators.note: about means placed around the other pieces

parts.note: natty means smartly dressed, well turned out

indicators.note: dismissed means the named letter is sent away

parts.note: IVF, in vitro fertilisation, is a treatment for infertility
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fertility treatment went well after the woman was sent home, ending in a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out well' looks like a story's happy ending; it is the adjective for smart dress. 'dismissed' sends the female's letter away from the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nativity is the birth of Christ, the occasion of a birth.
